wake3_native_task_read.title: HFO X12 Durable Object PDCA Lab

experiment.hypothesis: Across four wakes, the task contract fingerprint and exact task binding should remain stable even if the underlying carrier instance changes. Provider runtime timestamps may advance, but they do not identify the carrier.
experiment.strongest_falsifier: Wake 4 returns a different task-contract or schedule digest without authorized task mutation; a provider-exposed carrier field changes but is suppressed; provider runtime timestamps do not progress across a completed wake; the duplicate idempotency key is accepted; a stale expected version advances; or event/CURRENT readback fails.

canonical_transition.honest_flaw: This third observation adds only a stable task-contract fingerprint and advancing scheduler/task-record timestamps. Those timestamps describe provider bookkeeping and the prior completed wake, not the identity of the carrier executing this wake. Model build, worker instance, conversation identity, and Project context remain opaque, so carrier variance is still unmeasured and a stable contract can mask carrier changes. The event and CURRENT pointer are separate Git commits, and Slack follows both; GitHub's single-file blob-SHA guard does not provide cross-file atomicity, locks, linearizability, exactly-once execution, serializable transactions, database durability, Slack atomicity, or automatic orphan-event repair.
canonical_transition.rollback: Never delete the immutable event or Slack message. If later invalidated, append a compensating event from the then-current version and replace CURRENT only using that pointer file's exact then-current blob SHA.
